checksums.name: region_b_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: sum of 35 little-endian u32 words at offsets 0x08-0x93, plus two externally-sourced u32 words read from *_DAT_08029748 and _DAT_08029748[1] (not present in this static capture), stored as the 36th word at offset 0x94. Computed and written in-place immediately before the 144-byte flush.

checksums.name: region_c_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: sum of 87 little-endian u32 words at offsets 0x98-0x1F3, plus two externally-sourced u32 words read from *_DAT_0802979c and _DAT_0802979c[1] (not present in this static capture), stored as the 88th word at offset 0x1F4. Computed and written in-place immediately before the 352-byte flush.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic bit-serial DMA-style transfer primitive against the EEPROM MMIO data port (operand 0xD000000). Programs 3 transfer registers, sets a 0x80000000 enable bit, busy-waits on a 0x8000 status bit. No save-specific knowledge; shared by both read and write paths.

Reads one 8-byte (64-bit) EEPROM block: sends a bit-serial READ command then clocks back 68 bits, unpacking the last 64 data bits into the caller's output buffer. Bounds-checked against an address-bit-width table.
1-line wrapper calling 0x080365a0 with wait-for-completion flag set to 1.
Raw 8-byte EEPROM block write: sends bit-serial WRITE command (header+address+64 data bits+stop), then polls the EEPROM ready bit (uRam0d000000 & 1) with a scanline-count-based timeout (~228 ticks).
Write-verify: reads back the just-written 8-byte block via 0x080364dc and compares against the intended data; returns 0x8000 on mismatch.

Write-with-retry: up to 3 attempts of raw write (0x0803658c) followed by read-verify (0x08036700); breaks on first clean pair. Called indirectly as func_0x08036758 from 0x080297e0 (decompiled.c:2761); no further in-trace static caller resolved.
Multi-block reader: converts a byte offset to a block index and loops over ceil(len/8) calls to 0x080364dc, advancing by 1 block/8 bytes per iteration. Returns 1 on full success.

Multi-block writer: identical loop structure calling func_0x08036758 per 8-byte block. Returns 1 on full success. Sole bridge between game-level save buffers and EEPROM block I/O for all 3 writer entry points.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Save-validity check: reads the 8-byte header/magic block and compares both words against ROM constants.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Located the only in-trace call site of func_0x080297a0 (decompiled.c:2567), read the surrounding function body, confirmed callgraph.json has no other caller.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Header/magic write, invoked on save format / new-game initialization: stamps two ROM-constant words into the RAM mirror then flushes 8 bytes to EEPROM offset 0.
caller_chains.how_mapped: decompiled.c:2604-2624 directly assigns the two mirror words from ROM constants before calling func_0x080297e0(mirror,0,8); cross-checked against callgraph.json entry for 0x080297e0.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Region B payload save: sums 35 preceding words, adds 2 external RAM words, stores result as the 36th word, flushes 144 bytes to EEPROM offset 8.
caller_chains.how_mapped: decompiled.c:2631-2662; loop bound 0x23 and store index [0x23] confirmed arithmetically against the 0x90-byte flush length (36 words).

caller_chains.trigger_context: Region C payload save: sums 87 preceding words, adds 2 external RAM words, stores result as the 88th word, flushes 352 bytes to EEPROM offset 0x98.
caller_chains.how_mapped: decompiled.c:2669-2700; loop bound 0x57 and store index [0x57] confirmed arithmetically against the 0x160-byte flush length (88 words), and the stored word's absolute offset (0x1F4) matched a non-filler 4-byte value in the real .sav sample.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip byte 0x02 (part of ASCII "Mo" in the magic) from 0x4D to 0x00
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_08029654's word-compare fails; game should treat the save as absent/invalid and offer a fresh-game/format path.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change byte 0x1D (low byte of score_record_EDA's value field) from 0x7a to 0x00, then test both with and without recomputing region_b_checksum_word
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If score_record_EDA is really a displayed high-score value, the UI score table entry changes; comparing the repaired-checksum case against the unmodified-checksum negative control resolves whether region B's checksum is actually verified on load.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit in region_c_checksum_word without touching any region C data byte
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If an out-of-trace loader verifies this checksum, region C should be treated as corrupt/reset to default; no observable change would prove the checksum is write-only telemetry.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write non-0xFF bytes into the unused tail via external tooling, then perform a normal in-game save
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: A normal save should leave this range at 0xFF afterward (fresh/restore repeat), confirming no 4th writer exists outside the traced call set.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Play two sessions producing clearly different scores for two different tracked initials, diff the resulting .sav files across 0x10-0x8F
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Only the ranked-record counter/value fields for the affected initials should change, and secondary_tag_value_table's duplicated value should track the most recent score; any other change pattern falsifies the current HYPOTHESIS-level record layout.

open_questions: No read-side checksum verification/load routine was found for region B or region C within the 219 traced functions — only the write-and-generate side (FUN_080296fc, FUN_0802974c) and the region A magic read (FUN_08029654) exist in-trace.

The two external RAM addends folded into each checksum (via *_DAT_08029748/_DAT_0802979c and the following word) could not be resolved to concrete values from this static decompilation, so neither checksum could be numerically closed against the sample.

Region B's stored checksum word is exactly 0x00000000 in the only available sample, which does not obviously follow from the traced formula; could indicate this save was captured before region B was ever substantively written, an off-by-one in our understanding of the 36-word layout, or an unseen function that clears/overwrites this word.

Field-level semantics inside regions B and C (score records, the secondary tag/value table, and all UNKNOWN tail words) are inferred purely from repeating byte structure in one sample and are not corroborated by any traced code that manipulates individual sub-fields.

Only one real .sav sample exists in this workspace; a second, meaningfully different sample (or paired pre/post .ss save-states) is required to differentially confirm which bytes are load-bearing before any field can be promoted out of HYPOTHESIS.
